new_matches.title: IT Network Specialist
new_matches.description: About Allia Health Group Allia Health Group is a fast-growing digital health system revolutionizing metabolic, hormonal, and longevity care. As the parent organization behind Brello Health (women's telehealth and longevity programs), HelloWellness (men's telehealth), Southend Pharmacy (a state-licensed 503A compounding pharmacy), and Zito Care (our healthcare provider network), we deliver seamless, end-to-end care powered by a shared technology and AI platform. We remove barriers so clinicians can focus on patients and patients can access personalized, proactive care on their own terms — whether through telehealth visits, compounded medications, lab testing, wellness support, and more, all in one connected experience across 35+ states. Allia is building the future of healthcare by being clinician-first and patient-centered. We are innovative, empathetic, and accessible to our patients, combining cutting-edge tools with human-centered care to make high-quality longevity and wellness solutions affordable and available to more people. Why join us? At Allia Health Group, you're part of something bigger — helping shape a mission-driven enterprise that's scaling rapidly, solving real problems in healthcare inefficiencies, and making a tangible difference in people's lives every day. Position Summary Own the on-premise network and its security at the Southend Pharmacy compounding facility and across the infrastructure supporting our brands, working with the CTO organization’s cloud security team where site infrastructure meets cloud workloads. Beyond keeping things connected, this role builds the logging, alerting, and monitoring layer that lets us see security and availability events, which is our biggest blind spot today. Escalation and change approval run through the IT Operations Lead. Identity-integrated network access is coordinated with the Systems Administrator. Key Responsibilities Network Segmentation: Design and maintain zones that separate compounding production systems, PHI-bearing workstations, clinical devices, administrative users, and guest or BYOD traffic, which the 2026 HIPAA Security Rule expects. Firewall & Perimeter Management: Own the firewall rule lifecycle, including documented periodic review, change approval, and elimination of undocumented or overly permissive rules. Logging Architecture: Deploy and operate centralized log collection spanning firewalls, switches, wireless, servers, endpoints, and pharmacy production systems, with retention configured to the standard set by the compliance program. Alerting & Detection: Build tuned alert rules with clear severity tiers routed to a named responder. The goal is a manageable number of alerts that are worth acting on. Proactive Monitoring: Track throughput, latency, packet loss, and capacity on production-critical paths, watching trends so problems surface before they turn into outages. Site Connectivity & Redundancy: Manage carrier circuits and redundant paths for the pharmacy and supporting sites, and test failover on a schedule so we know it works. Wireless Infrastructure: Deploy enterprise wireless with certificate-based authentication and separate production, corporate, and guest SSIDs, tuned for the density of scanners and mobile devices on the production floor. Secure Remote Access: Administer VPN and Zero Trust network access for remote staff and offshore contractors, in coordination with the Systems Administrator (Identity & IAM). Vulnerability Management: Run regular scans of network-attached infrastructure and track fixes to closure, documenting risk acceptance where a fix is deferred. Technical Incident Response: Lead the technical side of security incidents, covering detection, triage, containment, eradication, and the write-up afterward. Pre-Authorized Containment: Act immediately on lower-severity events such as isolating an endpoint, disabling an account, or blocking an address, and notify afterward. Escalate to the IT Operations Lead when there is suspected PHI exposure, when an action would affect compounding production, or when an incident stays open past its severity clock. Configuration & Change Control: Version all network configurations, keep topology documentation current, and produce evidence supporting SOC 2 change-management controls. Circuit & Vendor Governance: Hold carriers and hardware vendors accountable to contracted service levels, and plan end-of-life refresh before equipment becomes an availability risk. Site Coverage Backup: Provide on-site coverage for the IT Support Specialist during absences or overlapping production incidents, following documented runbook procedures only. This role does not own tickets or work the standard support queue. Coverage: Standard hours are 08:00 to 17:00 CST, Monday through Friday, with participation in an on-call rotation for production-critical and security events outside those hours. IT Network Specialist — Qualifications Education Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, network engineering, or a related field preferred. Equivalent hands-on experience is accepted in place of a degree. Required Certifications CCNA, or equivalent vendor certification for comparable platforms (JNCIA, Aruba ACSA, Fortinet FCP), or demonstrated equivalent skill CompTIA Security+, or equivalent security fundamentals credential Preferred Certifications Firewall certification for Palo Alto PCNSA/PCNSE, Fortinet NSE, Cisco Firepower CWNA (Certified Wireless Network Administrator) Cisco CyberOps Associate, GIAC GCIH, or comparable incident response training Required Experience 5-8 years in network administration or network engineering At least 2 years owning a production network environment, including change decisions and escalation, rather than working assigned tickets within someone else's design Multi-site experience including carrier circuit management and redundant path failover Direct, hands-on firewall rule administration — creating, reviewing, and removing rules under a change process Enterprise wireless deployment and troubleshooting Strongly Preferred Experience Built centralized logging, monitoring, or SIEM capability from the ground up, including choosing what to collect, configuring retention, and tuning alerts. This is the highest-value qualification for this role. Network segmentation in a regulated or production environment — healthcare, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or PCI-scoped Wireless deployment supporting handheld scanners or mobile equipment in a warehouse, production floor, or clinical setting Participation in security incident response, including containment and post-incident documentation Producing evidence for compliance audits (HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI, HITRUST) Trainable — Not Required HIPAA and SOC 2 specifics, pharmacy operations, and USP 797/800 controlled-area procedures. Candidates with PCI, clinical, or manufacturing OT backgrounds carry transferable instincts and should not be screened out for lacking healthcare experience. What We Offer: Full benefits package including medical, vision, dental, 401(k) with company match, PTO, Flex days, holidays, and more! Allia Health Group does not provide employment visa sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship. Equal Opportunity Employer Statement Allia Health Group is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer where we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We are committed to cultivating a culture where all team members feel valued & respected. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, disability, age, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected by applicable law.

new_matches.title: Senior Core Infrastructure Engineer
new_matches.description: Job Description Designs, implements, and optimizes components in distributed systems with an emphasis on scalability, resiliency, and operability. Delivers features and load/performance tests; leverages data plane platforms and distributed state tools for high-volume retrieval, storage, and processing; and reviews peers’ implementations for scalability compliance. Builds fault-tolerant paths (redundancy, replication, automatic failover), applies recovery‑oriented principles, and implements retries, circuit breakers, and timeouts. Proactively detects and mitigates issues via tests, alarms, dashboards, and telemetry; authors runbooks and participates in incident response and RCAs. Implements standard replication and synchronization, develops automation/IaC for troubleshooting and maintenance, and applies advanced security controls (encryption, access, remediation) while ensuring change, compliance, and documentation standards are met. Responsibilities Key Responsibilities System Design & Architecture - System Scalability: –Implements and contributes to the development for components of distributed systems that support horizontal and vertical scaling including leveraging distributed state management tools. –Optimizes code and/or systems for large-scale data processing in large-scale systems. –Implements scalability requirements for assigned components and reviews implementation of team members. –Leverages components of data plane platforms to handle large-scale data retrieval, storage, and processing. –Implements performance and load testing. System Design & Architecture - System Reliability Design: –Collaborates with team to build fault-tolerant components capable of withstanding in-service updates by implementing redundancy, replication, and automatic failover mechanisms. –Applies recovery oriented computing principles to design components that effectively handle service disruptions. –Implements retry mechanisms, circuit breakers, and timeouts to help handle network unreliability. System Design & Architecture - System Reliability Performance: –Implements tests and alarm configurations to proactively detect and address issues/failures. –Supports efforts to recover from failures by drafting and executing runbooks and operational procedures. –Builds and customizes dashboards, telemetry systems, and alerting mechanisms to monitor component health. System Design & Architecture - Correctness / Availability: –Designs and implements functional requirements and testing for assigned features within an existing system. –Implements tests scenarios (e.g., fault-injection, brown-out) to evaluate system correctness. –Implements standard data replication and synchronization techniques to maintain data integrity and availability. Operational Troubleshooting & Incident Management: –Diagnoses, debugs, and resolves issues in system components to support ongoing operation. –Implements basic strategies to prevent interruptions, ensuring no maintenance windows are required for customers and users when resolving issues. –Designs and implements automation scripts and tooling used to troubleshoot operational issues. –Participates in operational support rotations, assisting in incident responses and root cause investigations. Compliance & Security: –Applies advanced security measures to protect data and applications in multi-tenant environments, including encryption and access controls. –Implements remediation plans to continuously improve security. –Collaborates with the team to ensure cloud infrastructure complies with relevant industry standards and regulations and that documentation is up-to-date Automation & Change Management: –Maintains automation scripts and tools (e.g., Infrastructure as Code (IaC)) for managing cloud infrastructure. –Adheres to change management plans for patching, updating, and rolling back applications. Core Responsibilities Planning & Execution: –Track timelines with minimal supervision, ensuring work is completed in a timely manner and is in alignment with project requirements. –Prioritize and adjust work as resources or timelines change, with some guidance Collaboration & Partnership: –Collaborates across teams to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives. Builds and maintains a comprehensive understanding of business, stakeholder, and/or customer needs to build and support effective partnerships. Actively listens to diverse perspectives and asks questions to ensure understanding of others. Problem Solving: –Independently identifies and addresses standard and non-standard issues in accordance with standard practices, escalating more complex issues as appropriate. Analyzes data and/or information from multiple sources to troubleshoot standard and non-standard errors. Contributes to knowledge sharing and best practices Continuous Learning: –Embraces continuous learning by actively seeking to build knowledge and new skills and/or tools, and staying current with industry trends and best practices. Seeks out and leverages feedback and training to improve skills. Contributes to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing with team members.. Continuous Improvement: –Develops ideas and recommends updates to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within a team. Seeks input from team members on alternative approaches and methods for improving work. Requirements: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, Computer Information Systems, Information Systems, Information Technology, Telecommunications, Mathematics, Physics, or related field AND 4 years of experience in software development OR Master's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Electrical/Electronics Engineering, Computer Information Systems, Information Systems, Information Technology, Telecommunications, Mathematics, Physics, or related field AND 2 year of experience in software development Qualifications Disclaimer: Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements. Range and benefit information provided in this posting are specific to the stated locations only US: Hiring Range in USD from: $79,200 - $209,500 per year. May be eligible for bonus and equity. Oracle maintains broad salary ranges for its roles in order to account for variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions and locations, as well as reflect Oracle's differing products, industries and lines of business. Candidates are typically placed into the range based on the preceding factors as well as internal peer equity. Oracle US offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes the following: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including expert medical opinion Short term disability and long term disability Life insurance and AD&D Supplemental life insurance (Employee/Spouse/Child) Health care and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts Pre-tax commuter and parking benefits 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company match Paid time off: Flexible Vacation is provided to all eligible employees assigned to a salaried (non-overtime eligible) position. Accrued Vacation is provided to all other employees eligible for vacation benefits. For employees working at least 35 hours per week, the vacation accrual rate is 13 days annually for the first three years of employment and 18 days annually for subsequent years of employment. Vacation accrual is prorated for employees working between 20 and 34 hours per week. Employees working fewer than 20 hours per week are not eligible for vacation. 11 paid holidays Paid sick leave: 72 hours of paid sick leave upon date of hire. Refreshes each calendar year. Unused balance will carry over each year up to a maximum cap of 112 hours. Paid parental leave Adoption assistance Employee Stock Purchase Plan Financial planning and group legal Voluntary benefits including auto, homeowner and pet insurance The role will generally accept applications for at least three calendar days from the posting date or as long as the job remains posted. We operate globally, recognize and reward talent, and work hard to keep SIOS a great place to work. SIOS is headquartered in San Mateo, CA, with offices across North America, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific. Our Columbia, SC office, located at the University of South Carolina Innovation Center, was recognized as one of the state’s best places to work in SC for the past 7 consecutive years.  What We Believe in: At SIOS Technology Corp., we believe our greatest strength is our ability to grow, collaborate, and innovate with a diverse team of employees in a positive, inclusive environment. The rich contributions that SIOS employees around the world make to our team are informed and enhanced by their individual differences, life experiences, traditions, values, and talents. We are committed to nurturing a culture of inclusion and connectedness among team members from different races, ethnicities, nationalities, religions, beliefs, genders, sexual orientations, ages, and disabilities. Position Overview: SIOS Technology Corp. is seeking a talented and enthusiastic Associate Product Support Engineer to join our fast-paced and fun Customer Experience Team located on the University of South Carolina campus (Columbia, SC). The Associate Product Support Engineer is the first line of contact for customers experiencing issues with installation, configuration, operation, and management of the SIOS solution. As an Associate Product Support Engineer, you will be part of a 7x24 Support Team focused on worldwide customer support for the SIOS family of high availability clustering and continuous data protection products. You will be responsible for providing phone and email support to end customers, resellers, system integrators, and partners for the industry’s best solution for ensuring uptime of business-critical applications. new_matches.title: Network & Wireless Engineer – Project Delivery
new_matches.description: Network & Wireless Engineer – Project Delivery VALL Technologies | Fort Collins, Colorado Full-Time | On-Site / Field-Based About the Role VALL Technologies is seeking a Network & Wireless Engineer who enjoys solving technical problems, working directly with customers, and taking ownership of projects from preparation through successful completion. This is not a narrowly defined network operations position. Our projects span enterprise networking, Wi-Fi, private wireless, fixed wireless, switching, routing, firewalls, and other communications infrastructure. Because we are a small engineering company, the person in this role will have meaningful responsibility and will work across engineering, deployment, troubleshooting, project coordination, and customer communication. We are looking for someone who takes pride in being dependable, prepared, technically capable, and easy to work with. You should enjoy learning unfamiliar technologies and be comfortable saying, “I haven’t worked with that before, but I’ll figure it out.” What You’ll Do You will help design, stage, configure, deploy, troubleshoot, and support customer networks. Typical responsibilities include: Configure and provision enterprise Wi-Fi access points, switches, routers, and firewalls Stage and validate equipment before customer deployments Configure and troubleshoot Ruckus wireless and ICX switching platforms Install and commission network hardware and software Troubleshoot Layer 1 through Layer 3 network issues Perform wireless troubleshooting and basic RF analysis Assist with Wi-Fi surveys, validation, optimization, and performance testing Work with VLANs, DHCP, routing, switching, PoE, VPNs, firewalls, and related network services Maintain accurate configurations, documentation, inventories, and project records Coordinate project activities and track open items through resolution Communicate directly with customers, vendors, manufacturers, and project partners Provide concise project updates identifying completed work, open items, roadblocks, and next steps Follow up proactively rather than waiting to be asked for status Travel to customer locations when projects require onsite engineering or deployment support Our work occasionally requires early mornings, evenings, maintenance windows, or longer days during deployments and critical customer events. These are not intended to be the everyday schedule, but flexibility is an important part of the position. What We’re Looking For Technical capability matters, but reliability and ownership matter just as much. The right person: Shows up on time and prepared Communicates clearly and professionally Takes ownership of assignments through completion Keeps customers and teammates informed without being chased for updates Identifies roadblocks early and asks for help when necessary Can organize multiple projects and priorities Pays attention to details Documents their work Enjoys troubleshooting difficult technical problems Is comfortable interacting directly with customers Maintains a friendly, professional demeanor, including when projects become stressful Is willing to perform both engineering and hands-on implementation work Is curious and willing to learn technologies outside their existing experience Technical Experience Strong candidates should have experience with several of the following: Enterprise Wi-Fi Ruckus Wireless or comparable enterprise WLAN platforms Ruckus ICX, Cisco, Aruba, Juniper, or comparable Ethernet switching VLANs and 802.1Q trunking Layer 2 switching and spanning tree IPv4 networking and subnetting Static and dynamic routing DHCP and DNS Firewalls, NAT, and VPNs PoE/PoE+/PoE++ Network troubleshooting using packet captures, CLI tools, and diagnostic utilities Wireless RF fundamentals including RSSI, SNR, channel utilization, interference, channel planning, and transmit power Network equipment staging, installation, testing, and commissioning Experience with CBRS/private LTE/5G, fixed wireless, microwave, fiber networks, RF design tools, or spectrum analysis is a plus but is not required. We would rather hire someone with strong fundamentals, initiative, and the ability to learn than someone who simply has a long list of certifications. Project & Customer Responsibility This is an important part of the position. Engineers at VALL Technologies interact directly with customers. You will be expected to understand what you are responsible for, know the status of your projects, communicate changes and roadblocks, and follow commitments through completion. If you prefer a position where someone else handles customers, schedules, project coordination, and follow-up while you concentrate exclusively on network configuration, this position probably isn’t the right fit. If you enjoy owning a technical problem and helping a customer get from “we have a problem” to “it’s working,” you may enjoy this role. Physical & Travel Requirements This position includes hands-on network deployment work. Candidates must be comfortable: Installing and replacing network equipment Working in equipment rooms, telecom closets, offices, and customer facilities Using basic hand tools Moving and installing typical networking equipment Traveling periodically for customer projects Occasionally working from ladders or at modest heights when necessary VALL Technologies does not operate a bucket truck, and tower or significant work-at-height activities are generally performed by specialized contractors. What Success Looks Like A successful engineer at VALL Technologies becomes someone our customers and team can depend on. When assigned a project, you understand the objective, prepare for the work, execute it professionally, communicate what happened, identify anything still outstanding, and make sure the project continues moving forward. You don’t need to know everything on your first day. You do need to care about getting things right. About VALL Technologies VALL Technologies is a Colorado-based wireless and network engineering company serving enterprise, municipal, education, hospitality, telecommunications, and other customers. We work across traditional IT networking and advanced wireless infrastructure, giving our engineers exposure to projects and technologies that are difficult to experience in a narrowly specialized networking position. We are a small company. That means individual performance matters, good work is visible, and engineers have an opportunity to take significant responsibility as their capabilities grow.

new_matches.title: Plant Engineer
new_matches.description: The Selkirk Cogeneration Station is a 446 MW natural gas-fired facility in Selkirk, New York, featuring three GE 7EA combustion turbines, one steam turbine, and four auxiliary boilers. Owned by Gate City Capital and operated by NAES Corporation, the plant provides reliable combined heat and power generation. New Athens Generating, located 30 miles south of Albany, is a 1,080 MW combined-cycle facility featuring three Siemens 501G combustion turbines. Opportunity Summary The Plant Engineer provides engineering, reliability, and technical support for Selkirk Cogeneration Station and New Athens Generating, helping improve plant performance, equipment reliability, and operational efficiency. Based at Selkirk, this role also leads the facility’s NERC compliance program, overseeing regulatory requirements, internal controls, documentation, and audit readiness. This position offers a unique opportunity to combine hands-on power generation engineering with significant NERC compliance leadership across two natural gas-fired generating facilities. As Plant Engineer, you will play a key role in the following areas: Engineering Performance & Reliability – Selkirk & New Athens Monitor plant equipment and performance, including combustion turbines, steam turbines, HRSGs, and auxiliary systems, analyzing heat rate, efficiency, and operating trends to improve reliability and performance. Investigate forced outages, generation losses, equipment failures, and operational events; perform root cause analyses and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence. Evaluate and optimize DCS, PLC, instrumentation, and measurement systems to support reliable equipment operation and accurate plant performance data. Support predictive and condition-based maintenance programs, including vibration analysis, thermography, and oil analysis, to identify equipment issues and improve reliability. Develop and maintain engineering procedures, drawings, technical specifications, and configuration documentation to ensure accurate plant records and effective configuration control. Coordinate with plant personnel, OEMs, engineering firms, and contractors to troubleshoot technical issues, implement equipment modifications, and develop scopes of work. Perform equipment reliability studies and design reviews, recommending improvements that increase availability, efficiency, capacity, and long-term plant performance. Manage capital and engineering projects from development through implementation, ensuring adherence to approved budgets, schedules, and contractual requirements. Provide engineering and technical support to Selkirk Cogeneration Station and New Athens Generating for plant performance, reliability, troubleshooting, and project needs. NERC Compliance & Program Administration – Selkirk Serve as Selkirk’s primary site lead for NERC compliance, overseeing applicable Operator and Owner compliance obligations and maintaining ongoing regulatory readiness. Manage Selkirk’s NERC Internal Control Program (ICP), including procedures, internal controls, compliance evidence, records, and required documentation. Monitor and interpret applicable NERC Reliability Standards and regulatory changes, assessing plant impacts and implementing necessary updates to programs, procedures, and controls. Manage NERC compliance documentation and reporting, including RSAWs, evidence packages, self-certifications, and other required records. Lead preparation for NERC audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory visits in coordination with NAES NERC personnel and other internal and external stakeholders. Identify compliance risks and gaps, manage corrective actions through completion, and maintain processes for tracking requirements, deadlines, and compliance responsibilities. Develop NERC compliance training and advise plant personnel and leadership on Reliability Standards, regulatory changes, compliance risks, and required actions. NAES Safe Safety is a core value at NAES, and as a condition of employment, all employees are expected to remain mentally alert and work safely at all times. Employees must also adhere to all safety warnings and posted signs while on company property. Additionally, they are required to follow all NAES safety rules and procedures. Adherence to these safety responsibilities is one of the key factors in the evaluation of each employee’s performance. Working Relationships The Plant Engineer reports to the Plant Manager and collaborates with plant leadership, Operations, Maintenance, and NAES Corporate resources on engineering, reliability, and NERC compliance activities. Physical Requirements And Working Conditions Physical requirements include standing for extended periods of time, climbing stairs and ladders, working from elevated platforms and walkways at varying heights, and routinely lifting up to 50 pounds. Power plant environment that may involve entering confined spaces, crawling through narrow areas, and handling hazardous materials, with exposure to fumes, extreme temperatures, and noise. Work may include high heat near equipment and varying outdoor weather conditions. Some duties may require the use of protective equipment, which can include hard hats, safety glasses, and eye protection, air masks/respirators, ear protection, chemical suits, flame-resistant clothing (FRC), hot gloves, high-voltage protective gear, and fall protection. Fit testing for respirators may be required. Strict smoking restrictions apply in and around the facility. Fitness for Duty All personnel will participate in the Fitness for Duty Program, which includes a post-offer physical examination, drug screening, and post-employment random drug screening. Work Schedule The Plant Engineer works a standard Monday to Friday day-shift schedule. This position will require extended hours, flexible shifts, weekends, holidays, and on-call availability as needed to support plant operations and business needs. Travel to New Athens Generating is required to provide engineering support, with occasional additional travel for Manager, Owner, User Group, or other offsite meetings. Compensation This position offers an annual base salary ranging from $145,000 to $157,000 and includes eligibility for an annual performance bonus. Professional Expertise & Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering field is required. Relevant power generation, industrial, or military experience may be considered in lieu of education. Demonstrated knowledge of power plant operations, maintenance, and engineering practices within natural gas-fired or similar power generation facilities. Experience investigating equipment failures, forced outages, and generation losses through root cause analysis and implementing corrective actions that improve reliability and plant performance. Strong experience administering NERC compliance programs within an operating power generation facility, including interpretation and application of applicable NERC Reliability Standards. Experience with NERC Generating Availability Data System (GADS) reporting is a plus. Experience managing NERC internal controls, compliance documentation, evidence, audit preparation, self-certifications, and corrective actions to maintain compliance and audit readiness. Proficiency with DCS/PLC platforms, plant instrumentation and measurement systems, and plant performance/data management systems such as OSIsoft PI; familiarity with CEMS/DAHS applications is preferred. Working knowledge of predictive and condition-based maintenance techniques, environmental regulations, and applicable power plant safety requirements. Strong analytical, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interpret technical and regulatory requirements, manage priorities, and effectively communicate findings and recommendations. Must possess a valid, unrestricted U.S. driver’s license and ensure it remains in good standing at all times. About NAES NAES Corporation is a leading provider of operations, maintenance, and engineering services for energy facilities. We serve clients across the power generation, oil and gas, and renewable energy sectors throughout North America and internationally, supporting the full life cycle of power generation and other industrial facilities. NAES is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are based on merit and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, military status, USERRA-protected status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
